label: YS-28
title: UI repoint after cutover is fully off-chain with no on-chain gate or timeout: premature broadcast leaves users on stale UI hitting reverts
description: CutoverAndRevokeOldMinter.s.sol atomically revokes OLD_MINTER's mint authority and client status in a single broadcast. The only safeguard ensuring the phoenix-ui is repointed before or immediately after cutover is a console.log reminder at lines 141-144 that directs the operator to run patch-mainnet-addresses-phusd-minter-replace.js and manually redeploy the phoenix-ui mainnet-addresses.ts (acknowledged as 'Q-REFS' in the NatSpec). There is no on-chain mechanism — no mandatory delay between Phase 2 and Phase 3, no timelock, no required pre-broadcast check that the UI has been updated — to prevent broadcasting the cutover while the live UI still points at OLD_MINTER. If the operator broadcasts Phase 3 before completing the UI repoint, every user who clicks mint on the stale UI will receive a revert (phUSD.mint: not authorized) until the UI is redeployed.
impact: User-facing mint availability gap between Phase 3 broadcast and UI redeployment completion. Funds are not at risk (mint reverts cleanly, no collateral is taken). Duration is bounded by how quickly the operator redeploys the UI, which could be minutes to hours depending on CI/CD pipeline.
recommendation: Add explicit operator checklist documentation at the top of CutoverAndRevokeOldMinter requiring the UI repoint to be confirmed complete BEFORE running Phase 3 broadcast. Consider running the off-chain patcher atomically in the migrate:phusd-minter-cutover npm script (chain the node patcher after the forge broadcast with &&) to reduce the window to seconds rather than minutes.
